report:
**Conclusion:** For children **over 1 year old** with an acute cough from a cold/upper-respiratory infection, honey may provide modest short-term relief—especially less nighttime coughing and better sleep for the child and caregiver. It appears at least as useful as many over-the-counter cough remedies, but the overall evidence is **low quality**, so it is symptom relief rather than a cure or treatment for the infection.

Do **not** give honey to infants under 12 months because of the risk of infant botulism. Seek medical advice promptly for breathing difficulty, bluish lips, dehydration, unusual drowsiness, a high/persistent fever, or cough that is severe or prolonged.

Sources:  
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/  
- https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng120/chapter/summary-of-the-evidence  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22869830/  
- https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children
